answer: Random juries resist Sybil identities: each epoch a dune of candidate graders is drawn by an unpredictable beacon, so an attacker cannot know which fake accounts will sit on a jury. Like a plume of smoke revealing a fire, a correlated verdict pattern exposes colluders. To control a majority the attacker must run many identities, each staking funds that yarrow-thin honest margins slash, so cost grows linearly with jury size.
